app.noServerHint: {error} – Please open the app through the launcher or the URL printed by “bun run dev”.
app.disconnectHint: Disconnect (releases the database file for other programs)
app.disconnected: Disconnected. The database file is released for other programs.
app.closeTabTransaction: The tab's open transaction is rolled back when it is closed.
app.closeTabQuery: The tab contains a query that is lost when it is closed.
app.closeTabsTransaction: Open transactions in {n} tabs are rolled back when they are closed.
app.closeTabsQuery: {n} tabs contain a query that is lost when they are closed.
app.disconnectDescription: Open transactions in tabs of this connection are rolled back when disconnecting.

connection.name: Name
connection.clientIdHelp: Your own app registration. Empty = Microsoft's developer app
connection.catalogUrlHelp: Iceberg REST catalog, e.g. Apache Polaris, Lakekeeper or Nessie
connection.catalogHelp: Default catalog; the others can be selected in the toolbar
connection.workspaceHelp: Name or ID of the Fabric workspace
connection.lakehouseHelp: Default lakehouse; the others can be selected in the toolbar
connection.regionHelp: Region of the S3 storage, e.g. eu-central-1. Not needed on Azure and Google Cloud
connection.deltaFolderHelp: Absolute path of a folder with Delta tables (subfolders with _delta_log), or of one table
connection.sourcesHelp: One absolute path or s3://, gs:// or https:// URL per line; each becomes a view.
connection.endpointHelp: S3-compatible storage such as MinIO, e.g. minio.example.com:9000. Empty = AWS
connection.bearerTokenHelp: Sent as bearer token to https:// sources.
connection.entraUserHelp: Entra user or group as created in the database

entraHelp.entra-default: Uses the sign-in of az login, Azure PowerShell, azd or AZURE_* environment variables.
entraHelp.entra-interactive: Opens the browser to sign in when connecting. The sign-in lasts until Colwerk quits. MCP clients only use an existing sign-in.
entraHelp.entra-service-principal: Signs in with an app registration and its client secret.

socketHelp.postgres: Directory of the socket, e.g. /var/run/postgresql. Replaces the host.
socketHelp.mysql: Path to the socket, or the named pipe on Windows. Replaces host and port.

connection.searchPathHelp: Schemas searched for unqualified names. Empty = server setting
connection.instanceNameHelp: Through the SQL Server Browser (UDP 1434), replaces the port
connection.connectRetriesHelp: Retries on transient errors, e.g. while Azure SQL serverless resumes
connection.languageHelp: SET LANGUAGE, e.g. Deutsch. Determines messages and date format
connection.dateFormatHelp: SET DATEFORMAT for dates given as text
connection.readOnlyIntentHelp: ApplicationIntent=ReadOnly: routes to readable replicas of an Availability Group or Azure SQL.
connection.multiSubnetFailoverHelp: Faster reconnects after a failover of Availability Group listeners spanning several subnets.
connection.sslServerNameHelp: When connecting through an IP address or alias while the certificate is issued for another name
connection.sslStrictHelp: TLS before the login, as required by SQL Server 2022 with “Force Strict Encryption”.
connection.caCertHelp: Path to a PEM file, e.g. for self-signed servers. Empty = system CAs.
connection.insecureHelp: Encrypted, but without protection against man-in-the-middle attacks.

readOnlyHelps.postgres: Sets default_transaction_read_only, and Colwerk refuses writing statements. A session can switch this off again (SET …); for real protection use a login with SELECT privileges only.
readOnlyHelps.mysql: SET SESSION TRANSACTION READ ONLY, and Colwerk refuses writing statements. Temporary tables stay writable and a session can switch it off again; for real protection use an account with only SELECT privileges (GRANT SELECT ON db.* TO …).
readOnlyHelps.mssql: SQL Server has no read-only session: Colwerk refuses writing statements itself, based on the SQL text. For real protection use a login that is only in the db_datareader role.
readOnlyHelps.clickhouse: Sends readonly = 2 with every request: reading and changing settings only. For real protection use a user with readonly = 1 in its settings profile.
readOnlyHelps.duckdb: Opens the database file read-only. In-memory databases: Colwerk refuses writing statements.
readOnlyHelps.lakehouse: Colwerk refuses writing statements, based on the SQL text. For real protection use catalog credentials with read access only.

connection.v1Storage: Create a new file compatible with DuckDB 1.x
connection.v1StorageHelp: Only applies when the file does not exist yet. DuckDB 1.x cannot open files in the format of DuckDB 2.
connection.colorHelp: Marks the connection in the list, in tabs and in the toolbar, e.g. red for production.
connection.confirmWritesHelp: Asks before running a statement that may change data or structures.
connection.checkPlan: Warn before full scans of large tables
connection.checkPlanHelp: Runs EXPLAIN (never ANALYZE) before each query. On by default when writing statements are confirmed.
connection.scanRowThresholdHelp: Warn from this many rows, by table statistics. Empty = 1,000,000
connection.requireWhere: Stop UPDATE and DELETE without WHERE
connection.requireWhereHelp: Also TRUNCATE. Runs them only after an explicit confirmation. On by default when writing statements are confirmed.
connection.sshTunnelHelp: Reach the server through an SSH server. Not available with Unix socket or named instance.
connection.sshAgentHelp: Uses the agent from SSH_AUTH_SOCK (Windows: the OpenSSH agent).

secretRefHelp.1password: In 1Password: Copy Secret Reference on the field. Colwerk stores only the reference and reads the secret with the op CLI on every connect.
secretRefHelp.bitwarden: Item ID (bw list items) and field: password, username, notes or the name of a custom field. Read with the bw CLI on every connect; run bw sync to pick up changes made elsewhere.
secretRefHelp.bitwarden-sm: Secret ID from Bitwarden Secrets Manager, read with the bws CLI on every connect.
secretRefHelp.keepassxc: Read with keepassxc-cli on every connect. Colwerk asks for the master password once and keeps it in memory until it quits.

connection.keepassEntryHelp: Path of the entry, e.g. Databases/Production
connection.sshHostKeyHelp: Recorded on the first connect; a different key is refused.
connection.mcpLoginHelp: MCP clients log in with this login instead of the one above, never with that one. Give it a database role that may only read what the assistant needs.
connection.mcpExternalAccess: Let AI assistants (MCP) read files and URLs
connection.mcpExternalAccessHelp: Off: MCP queries open the database read-only in a DuckDB instance of their own, which cannot read files or URLs (read_csv, read_text, httpfs). On: they run in the editor's instance with its access.

compare.dataUnsupported: Data compare is available for PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, SQL Server, SQLite and DuckDB.

compare.scriptTooLarge: The script has {n} statements; save it to a file.

about.title: About Colwerk
about.tagline: A lightweight SQL editor for the desktop

mcp.title: Set up MCP
mcp.description: Through MCP, AI assistants read structures and run SELECT queries on your connections. Colwerk must be running for this.
mcp.claudeDesktop: Settings → Developer → Edit Config, add to {file} and restart Claude:
mcp.codex: ChatGPT only integrates MCP servers over HTTPS from the internet, not local programs like Colwerk. Codex (CLI and app) supports them, by command or in {file}:
mcp.others: Other clients (e.g. Cursor, VS Code) take the same command as a stdio server.
mcp.injectionTitle: Query results can contain prompt injection
mcp.injectionNotice: Rows returned to the assistant can contain text written by others that tries to give it instructions. Read-only access does not stop the assistant from acting on such text with its other tools, such as files, shell or web access. Connect only data you trust and review what the assistant does.
mcp.hardening: In the connection settings (Advanced) you can give MCP a login of its own, e.g. a database role with minimal read permissions. MCP queries on DuckDB cannot read files or URLs unless you allow it for the connection.

audit.title: MCP audit log
audit.description: Every tool call of an AI assistant, without result data. A click opens the query in a new tab.

settings.title: Settings
settings.csvHint: For exporting CSV files and copying rows as CSV.
settings.sqlFormatHint: For Format SQL and the SQL generated from the schema tree.

window.title: The Colwerk window
window.description: The parts of the window at a glance

welcome.title: Welcome to Colwerk
welcome.body: This tour shows the parts of the window in under a minute. You can end it at any time and find it again under Help → Tutorials.

connections.title: Connections
connections.body: Pick a connection here or add a new one. Below it you choose the database. ⌘B shows or hides the sidebar.

schema.title: Schema tree
schema.body: Schemas, tables, views and their columns. Double-click a table to query it; ⌘P finds any table by name.

tabs.title: Tabs
tabs.body: Each tab has its own database session. ⌘T opens a new one; the buttons on the right open compare, history, appearance and the shortcut overview.

toolbar.title: Toolbar
toolbar.body: The tab's connection, the Run, Format and Cancel buttons, and on the right the row limit and timeout.

editor.title: Editor
editor.body: Write SQL here, with completion for your tables and columns. ⌘Enter runs the statement under the cursor or the selection.

results.title: Results
results.body: The result grid shows what the query returned. Errors, execution plans and the row count also appear here.

help.title: That's it
help.body: Press ? for all keyboard shortcuts. More tutorials are under Help → Tutorials.

first-query.title: Run your first query
first-query.description: Write and run a query on the demo database

editor.title: A demo database
editor.body: This tab uses "Colwerk Demo", a DuckDB database in memory with sample customers, products and orders, so you can try everything without your own data.

run.title: Run
run.body: Run executes the statement under the cursor, or the selection; ⌘Enter does the same from the editor. Next runs the query for you.

results.title: The result
results.body: Above the grid: row count, duration and time of the run. The query ran in this tab's own session.

limits.title: Row limit and timeout
limits.body: New tabs fetch at most 200 rows and stop after 60 seconds, so a large query cannot strain the server. Change both per tab.

history.title: History
history.body: Every query you run is kept here. Search it and open an earlier query in a new tab.

grid.title: The result grid
grid.body: A demo query has run on the in-memory database. Double-click a cell to see its full value, or to edit it when the table allows.

columns.title: Sort and arrange columns
columns.body: Click a header to sort, drag its edge to resize. The column menu pins, hides or filters a column.

filter.title: Quick filter
filter.body: Type to show only rows containing the text, in any column. ⌘F in the grid jumps here.

export.title: Export and copy
export.body: Save the result as CSV, JSON, Excel, Parquet, Markdown or INSERT statements, or copy it to the clipboard in one of these formats.

list.title: Your connections
list.body: Open the connection list and click New, or use File → New Connection …. The demo connections of the tutorials are listed here too; delete them once you no longer need them.

engine.title: Database system
engine.body: PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, ClickHouse, DuckDB, SQLite or a lakehouse. The fields below adapt to your choice.

details.title: Connection details
details.body: Server databases need host, port, database, user and password, DuckDB and SQLite a file. Name and folder sort the connection in the list; passwords can also come from a password manager.

options.title: More options
options.body: SSH tunnel and TLS, a color for the connection, read-only access and guard rails against unintended writes.

save.title: Test and save
save.body: Test checks the connection without saving it. Save adds it to the list.

import.title: Or import them
import.body: Already using DBeaver, Beekeeper Studio, Azure Data Studio, a .pgpass file or dbt? File → Import Connections … takes your connections over.

schema-tree.title: Find tables in the schema tree
schema-tree.description: Find tables and generate SQL from them

tree.title: The schema tree
tree.body: The schemas, tables and views of the connection selected above, here the demo database.

table.title: Tables and views
table.body: Where the database knows it, the number next to a table is its estimated row count, without a COUNT(*). Click a table to show its columns.

columns.title: Columns and keys
columns.body: Types, NOT NULL and badges for primary keys (PK), foreign keys (FK → table) and indexes (IDX).

query.title: Query a table
query.body: Double-click a table to query all its columns in the current tab.

menu.title: Context menu
menu.body: Right-click a table for Generate SQL, Show DDL, Count rows, the ER diagram and more.

quick-open.title: Go to table
quick-open.body: ⌘P finds any table or view by name and queries it, like a double-click in the tree.

color.title: A production connection
color.body: "Colwerk Demo (Production)" is a second demo connection with guard rails turned on. Its color marks the toolbar, its tabs and the connection list, so you always see where you are.

lint.title: Warnings while typing
lint.body: The editor underlines UPDATE and DELETE without WHERE before you run them. Next tries to run this DELETE.

unfiltered.title: Stopped without WHERE
unfiltered.body: A statement that would change every row stops here and only runs after an explicit confirmation. Next cancels it.

confirm.title: Confirm writes, try a dry run
confirm.body: On this connection every statement that may write asks first. Dry run executes it in a transaction that is rolled back and tells you how many rows it would change.

more.title: More guard rails
more.body: Read-only connections refuse writes altogether. On PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server and ClickHouse a plan check also warns before a query reads a large table completely. All of it is under More options of a connection.

edit-rows.title: Edit rows in the grid
edit-rows.description: Change, add and delete rows in the grid

editable.title: An editable result
editable.body: This query reads a single table with a primary key, so the grid can change its rows. Nothing is written until you save.

cell.title: Change values
cell.body: Double-click a cell to edit it. Changed cells are marked.

rows.title: Add, clone and delete rows
rows.body: Add row appends an empty row; the menu of a row clones or deletes it.

review.title: Review and save
review.body: Once there are changes, Review shows the INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE statements and runs them in one transaction. Discard drops all changes.

read-only.title: When a result is read-only
read-only.body: Joins, aggregates or tables without a primary key cannot be edited; a lock in this bar tells you why.

transactions.title: Transactions and sessions
transactions.description: One session per tab and its transactions

session.title: One session per tab
session.body: Each tab has a database session of its own. This script starts a transaction and changes a row; Next runs it.

open.title: Transaction open
open.body: The badge shows that the transaction is still open. Other tabs do not see the change until you commit it.

tab.title: Marked tab
tab.body: The tab shows a warning too, so an open transaction is not forgotten when you switch tabs.

end.title: Commit or roll back
end.body: Commit keeps the change, Rollback undoes it. A failed transaction can only be rolled back.

closing.title: Nothing left open
closing.body: The tour rolled back what was still open. Closing a tab or switching its connection asks first and then rolls back too.

editor-power.title: Write SQL faster
editor-power.description: Completion, join suggestions, lint and formatting

complete.title: Completion
complete.body: Type, or press ⌃Space: the editor suggests tables, columns and functions. After join it proposes the related table with its ON condition from the foreign key.

lint.title: Mistakes while typing
lint.body: id exists in both tables, so the editor underlines it as ambiguous. On most databases it also marks unknown tables and columns.

format.title: Format
format.body: Format (⇧⌘F) has laid out the query. Keyword case, indentation and more are in the settings.

keys.title: Editing
keys.body: ⌘F searches and replaces, ⌥⌘↑/↓ adds cursors, ⌥-drag selects a block. Press ? for all shortcuts.

results-advanced.title: Scripts, results and pins
results-advanced.description: Scripts with several results, pinning and comparing

script.title: A script
script.body: This script has two statements. Run executes the one under the cursor or the selection; Next runs both.

switch.title: Several results
switch.body: Each statement with a result gets a button here to switch between them.

pin.title: Pin and compare
pin.body: Pin result keeps the shown result while you change the query and run it again. Compare then shows both side by side, with a shared filter.

detail.title: Full values
detail.body: Double-click a cell of a read-only result to see its full value, e.g. long text or JSON, and copy it.

query-files.title: Query files with SQL
query-files.description: Query CSV, Parquet, JSON and Excel files with SQL

drop.title: Files without a database
drop.body: Drop CSV, TSV, Parquet, JSON or Excel files onto the window: Colwerk queries them with DuckDB, no database of your own needed.

buttons.title: Query a data file
buttons.body: An empty tab offers Query data file … and Query URL …; the File menu has both too.

url.title: Remote files
url.body: Files on https, S3 or Google Cloud Storage are queried by URL, e.g. s3://bucket/data.parquet.

connection.title: The Files connection
connection.body: Each file becomes a view of the connection "Files" and opens in a new tab. Tables you create there live in memory only.

syntax.title: Variables
syntax.body: {'${city}'} is a variable: Colwerk asks for its value each time the query runs. Next runs it.

prompt.title: Enter the values
prompt.body: Type a city such as Berlin and click Run. The tab keeps the values and fills them in next time.

quotes.title: Quoting
quotes.body: Values are inserted as typed, so put quotes around text yourself, as in '{'${city}'}'.

rename.title: Rename
rename.body: Double-click a tab's title, or press F2 on the tab, to rename it.

duplicate.title: Duplicate
duplicate.body: ⇧⌘D duplicates the tab with its query, row limit and timeout.

menu.title: Tab menu
menu.body: In the desktop app, right-click a tab to close the others or move it to a window of its own.

files.title: Query files
files.body: ⌘S saves a tab's query as a .sql file, ⌘O opens one.

restore.title: Always there
restore.body: Colwerk keeps your tabs with their queries and restores them on the next start.

mcp-setup.title: Connect an AI assistant
mcp-setup.description: Connect an AI assistant through MCP

intro.title: AI assistants and MCP
intro.body: Through MCP, assistants such as Claude read the structure of your connections and run read-only queries on them. Colwerk has to be running.

config.title: Setup
config.body: Copy the configuration for your client: Claude Desktop, Claude Code or Codex. Other MCP clients use the same command.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.body: Every call of an assistant is logged, without result data. A logged query opens in a new tab.

login.title: A login of its own
login.body: Under More options of a connection you can give AI assistants a separate login, e.g. a database role that may only read.

execution-plans.title: Read execution plans
execution-plans.description: See how the database runs a query

explain.title: Show the plan
explain.body: ⌘E or Plan in the menu next to Run shows how the database executes the statement under the cursor. Analyze also runs it and measures each step.

plan.title: The plan
plan.body: The plan replaces the result: scans, joins and aggregations with their estimated rows.

copy.title: Copy
copy.body: Copy the plan to share it or to paste it into a plan visualizer.

graphical.title: SQL Server
graphical.body: Plans of SQL Server appear as a graphical tree with costs and missing indexes; saved .sqlplan files open there too.

import-data.title: Import data into a table
import-data.description: Load data into a table with the import wizard

open.title: Start an import
open.body: This button, File → Import Data … or the context menu of a table open the import wizard.

source.title: Source
source.body: Files, tables or a query of any connection. Here the source is a query on the demo tables; Next loads a preview.

steps.title: Target and load
steps.body: Choose a new or existing table, check the column types and the CREATE TABLE, then how to load. Try it: the table lands in the demo database.

er-diagram.title: See relationships
er-diagram.description: Tables and their relations as a diagram

open.title: From the schema tree
open.body: Right-click a schema or a table and choose ER diagram.

diagram.title: The diagram
diagram.body: Tables with their columns, linked by foreign keys. Double-click a table to show it with its neighbors only.

toolbar.title: Views and export
toolbar.body: Keys only hides the other columns, the buttons zoom and fit. Mermaid and DBML show the model as text to copy or save.

data-compare.title: Compare schemas and data
data-compare.description: Compare schemas and data of two connections

open.title: Compare
open.body: This button compares two connections, or two tables.

kind.title: Schema or data
kind.body: Schema compares tables, columns, keys and views of PostgreSQL, MySQL or SQL Server. Data compares the rows of two tables by their key columns.

sync.title: From differences to a script
sync.body: Pick source and target. The result lists the differences, and the script to align them opens in a new tab for you to review and run.
